note: Track home-and-colour, mix step 5: Do or La as home, mixed: the chord on Do against the chord on La (chord tokens, counted the long way once), tunes of the learner's own that end on either, then a backing track in a new key whose four lines rest on Do or La out of turn. The key is moves (any key): the old Key selector is gone, the key is named as {{=key}}, and the last section's line says what stays the same in the new key. Missing: backing-track plays a fixed order, so the homes can't come at random.

exercise.title: Do or La: which note is home
exercise.why: A major key and a minor key can use the same seven notes and rest on different ones, Do or La, so the note where the music comes to rest tells you which of the two you are hearing.

cells.text:
{{chord:I}} is the 1st chord of {{=key}} major, built on Do, and {{chord:vi}} is the 6th chord, built on La. Both are made of notes of {{=key}} major: the one on Do is major, the one on La is minor.
Press a chord box below to hear the chord, and go between the two.
Practice until you can say "Do" or "La" from the sound alone.

cells.heading: End on Do, end on La

cells.text:
The staff below shows {{=key}} major with its solfège names, and the notes under the lowest Do as well. Tap a short tune of your own that ends on a ringed {{1}}, then one from the same notes that ends on a ringed {{6}}.
Practice until you can hum the last note of each tune before you tap it.

Press Play under the staff below to start the backing track, in a new key a step higher: sixteen bars in four lines, and each line comes to rest on Do or on La, not in turn. Hum the note each line rests on, then tap {{1}} or {{6}} on the staff to check.
Practice until you can call out "major" or "minor" as each line ends.
In the new key the notes are new, and a line that rests on Do still sounds major, one that rests on La still minor.
